jobs.title: Firmware Engineer
jobs.description_text: Company Overview Allen Control Systems (ACS) is a cutting-edge defense startup founded by two former Navy electrical engineers with a proven track record in robotics and software. We are developing an autonomous gun turret using advanced computer vision and control systems to precisely detect, track, and neutralize enemy drones. With an engineering-first culture, ACS values technical excellence and innovation. Backed by our founders’ successful exits from two previous ventures acquired for a combined $180M in 2022, we are committed to ensuring that the groundbreaking technologies we develop will have a real-world impact. About The Role We are looking for a Firmware Engineer to own the low-level embedded software that runs our autonomous aircraft in the field. This is a deep individual contributor role for someone with 4+ years of industry experience who can operate at the architecture and design level from day one. You will make real decisions about bare-metal versus RTOS tradeoffs, sensor and peripheral integration, deployment strategies for fielded aircraft, and the HIL testing infrastructure that validates it all. You are expected to document and justify those decisions with the same rigor you apply to the code itself. What You’ll Do - Own the architecture and implementation of time- and safety-critical embedded firmware on STM32-based platforms; evaluate existing firmware ecosystems and make well-reasoned decisions about what to carry forward versus redesign from scratch.

Bedrock's Behavior ML team builds the learned policies that decide what our machines actually do, and diffusion policies are a central bet: models that can represent the full distribution of expert behavior instead of averaging it into mush. During your internship you’ll be tasked with important problems for the business and expected to deliver just like any other full-time member of the team. In this role, you’ll help launch new growth-oriented partnerships, support existing partner operations, and improve financial and operational processes across the business. At Base, partnerships aren’t siloed – you’ll collaborate closely with Deployments, Growth, Software, and Hardware to deliver results that matter. jobs.title: Product, Member Experience
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE You'll sit at the intersection of product management and member lifecycle education—owning the post-sale member experience from the moment someone signs with Base through years of membership. Our members make a meaningful commitment when they join Base. Your job is to make sure they never regret it. That means getting ahead of their questions before they have them, guiding them through onboarding and installation with clarity, and continuously deepening their understanding of and engagement with their Base system. You'll own every product experience members touch in the app and dashboard, all post-sale automated communications sequences, the Help Center, and more. You will build something category-defining from the ground up. If you've worked in product, product marketing, or customer experience and you're tired of watching the same friction points resurface release after release, this role lets you fix it for everyone for good. Structured systems thinking and tactical execution are the core components of the job, not a skill you bring to someone else's roadmap. Done well, this role directly reduces contact volume, increases net promoter score, drives app engagement, and keeps members for life. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Product
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a senior or staff-level, product-minded engineer to lead development of the customer experience at Base. Our apps help members understand their energy usage, manage outages, and track the performance of the battery powering their home. You will set the architecture and technical direction of the interfaces that connect real-world energy systems with a clear, simple digital experience - and you’ll be the technical anchor others build on. You’ll join a small, high-impact team responsible for the digital front door of Base. In this role, you will lead development of major product surfaces across web and mobile, set technical direction across the frontend org, partner closely with product and design to shape the roadmap, and ensure we ship fast, reliable software. This role requires strong product judgment, technical leadership, and the ability to translate complex systems into simple experiences that millions of households can rely on. What You’ll Do - Lead development of the customer experience across Base web and mobile applications - Set frontend architecture and technical strategy across multiple product surfaces, not just your own - Define and evolve frontend architecture that supports a fast, reliable, and scalable product platform - Own major product surfaces end-to-end, from initial concept through production and iteration - Work closely with backend engineers to design APIs and data models that support product features - Translate comple

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Backend
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We're building BaseOS — the operating system that runs the modern power company. It coordinates thousands of distributed batteries, powers our internal operations, and enables us to deliver reliable, low-cost electricity at scale. As a senior, staff, or principal engineer on this team, you won't just build services — you'll define how the system works. You'll make architectural calls that other engineers build on top of, set the technical bar for the team, and take end-to-end ownership of the systems Base depends on every day. You'll be trusted to operate with minimal oversight on ambiguous, high-stakes problems — and to know which problems are worth solving in the first place. Your decisions will directly shape how power flows across the grid. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own critical systems at scale: Design, build, and operate the core services BaseOS runs on. You're accountable for their reliability, performance, and long-term direction — not just their uptime today - Set architecture and standards: Make foundational decisions on system design, data models, and service boundaries across teams. jobs.title: Environmental Health & Safety Engineer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base is seeking a EH&S Engineer to support our field operations teams in Texas. As an EHS Engineer, you will perform hazard assessments, incident investigations, work through employees’ safety concerns and issues, as well as strategize with site leaders to prevent/reduce injuries. In addition, you will ensure environmental compliance with all local, state, and federal regulatory requirements applicable to these departments. jobs.title: Environmental Health & Safety Technician
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base is growing fast and so is the infrastructure behind it. As an EHS technician, you'll be at the center of our safety program: on the floor, in the field, and deep in the compliance work that keeps our people safe and our operations running. jobs.title: Manager, Supplier Development Engineering
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Supplier Industrialization Engineering Manager to join our team. Base is an incredibly data driven organization which extends directly into our supply chain. We want to know the efficiencies and deficiencies of our suppliers just as well, if not better, than our own factories. This role focuses on ensuring that suppliers' manufacturing processes are optimized for the production of high-quality, cost-effective products. You will work closely with suppliers and internal teams to drive product and process improvements, manage supply chain issues, and ensure successful integration of new products into mass production. As a player-coach, you will also lead and develop a team of Supplier Development Engineers - staying hands-on in the technical work while growing the capabilities and careers of your team. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead and develop a team of Supplier Industrialization Engineers, balancing direct technical contribution with coaching, prioritization, and team growth. - Ramp supplier lines from early prototyping through full-scale production, ensuring readiness across equipment, staffing, and processes. - Size-up suppliers to see if they are a cultural fit to work with Base on a long-term basis. - Work directly with suppliers to assess, design, and optimize manufacturing processes to meet production requirements. jobs.title: Operations Manager (Connecticut)
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base is looking for an Operations Manager to lead our Connecticut market. This is a foundational leadership role responsible for the full operational footprint in the Northeast: warehouse and materials operations, field installation crews, and local market strategy. You will own the end-to-end execution of getting Base systems into homes—from the moment parts arrive at our warehouse to the moment a customer’s battery is energized. The ideal candidate brings a "builder’s mindset"—someone who is equally comfortable on the warehouse floor, on a job site, and in a high-level planning meeting. This role is about laying the groundwork for long-term success and setting the standard for excellence in service delivery. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Regional Leadership: Own all operational outcomes for Connecticut, including installation volume, warehouse throughput, quality, safety, and customer experience. - Market Strategy & Scaling: Translate company-wide goals into local execution plans. Identify "signals" in the data to improve local performance and design processes that can scale from 10 to 1,000+ installs. - Warehouse & Logistics: Supervise warehouse operations, ensuring 100% inventory accuracy (FIFO), WMS hygiene, and seamless material staging for field crews. - Field Operations: Manage and mentor field installation crews and electrical leads. This role supports our team, provides a friendly face to guest and team members alike, helps get the vendors coordinated and guided to the correct area or assigned to the correct team member, and keeps the culture strong. With your support, the rest of the team can focus on their work and be more efficient. This is a high visibility, high trust role. You'll be the first point of contact for guests, onboarding, and employees when it comes to the factory environment, and the person other teams count on to keep the space welcoming and organized. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the front desk and serve as the first point of contact for employees, visitors, candidates, vendors and other guests. - Coordinate onsite visits, notify interview panels when interviewers arrive, making sure everyone is welcomed and follows the the sign-in procedures. - Keep the reception area, conference rooms and shared spaces clean, and ensure they are organized, stocked, and ready for employees and visitors. - Support employee onboarding sessions, workplace events, and other day-to-day activities. - Work closely with the broader Workplace team, IT, Security, and HR in order to assist different needs. jobs.title: Finance - Planning Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a Financial Planning Intern to work closely with our finance team on budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and financial analysis. You’ll help bring together financial and operational information to better understand how the business is performing and where it is headed. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working with numbers, asking questions, and turning data into clear insights. You’ll have exposure to a broad range of financial planning activities and work closely with teams across the company. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Support budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes. - Help prepare and maintain financial reports and analyses. - Analyze actual results against budgets and forecasts and help identify key drivers of variances. - Work with financial and operational data to support business decisions. - Help organize and improve financial models, reporting, and planning processes. - Partner with members of the finance and accounting teams to understand and validate financial information. - Assist with recurring reporting and ad hoc analyses as the business evolves. - Help improve the way financial information is organized, accessed, and communicated across the company. jobs.title: Accounting Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for an Accounting Intern to get hands-on experience across the core of what our accounting team does day to day. You'll support month-end close, help keep the books accurate, and get exposure to how accounts payable, accounts receivable, reconciliations, and reporting actually work at a fast-growing company — not just the theory from a textbook. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants real reps on the fundamentals: journal entries, reconciliations, and the discipline of making sure every number ties out. You'll also have room to bring fresh thinking to how we work — using AI tools to speed up manual tasks and automate reconciliations, and helping develop and enhance our monthly reporting processes. You'll work closely with the accounting team, learn how the close runs today, and take on real pieces of it yourself. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Assist with month-end close tasks, including journal entries and account reconciliations. - Help reconcile bank accounts, credit card activity, and intercompany transactions. - Use AI tools to streamline manual, repetitive accounting tasks and help automate reconciliations. - Help develop and enhance our monthly reporting processes, making them faster and more reliable. - Assist with fixed asset tracking and depreciation schedules. - Help prepare supporting schedules for audits and tax filings. - Maintain organized, accurate documentation for accounting processes and controls. - Assist with ad hoc analysis and proj

jobs.title: Marketing Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE As a Marketing Intern, you'll join our Go-To-Market (GTM) team, gaining practical experience in marketing, from campaigns to member acquisition. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Help execute go-to-market strategies to improve member acquisition. - Build and maintain relationships with members, ensuring a positive member experience. - Analyze member interactions and campaign performance using HubSpot and other tools. - Work with the marketing team to hit campaign goals and improve the funnel. - Research target segments and help launch marketing campaigns to generate inbound leads. - Support outbound efforts alongside the sales team. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Interest in members, marketing, and relationship building. - Understanding of technology marketing and software products. - Strong communication skills in English, both verbal and written. - Ability to provide good member service and build rapport with clients. PREFERRED SKILLS - Familiarity with HubSpot (or other CRM systems) and Zapier. - Relevant experience. ABOUT THE TEAM The Growth team sets the pace for how fast Base can deliver affordable, reliable power to the people who need it. We operate as one team across marketing, sales, support, product, and design, lean and high-ownership. Everything we build comes back to one question: are we solving people's problems? We're building the world's most beloved company.

jobs.title: Deployments Operations Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE The Deployments Operations team is responsible for the logistics and coordination that make Base installs happen on time and on schedule—managing scheduling, crew coordination, inventory flow, and communication across field, warehouse, and customer touchpoints. We solve the difficult, high-impact problems that determine whether crews show up to job sites ready to work. Joining this team means owning processes that directly impact Base's ability to scale and deliver on its mission. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Support scheduling and coordination of installation appointments across field crews and customers. - Help track inventory and equipment logistics to ensure crews have what they need, when they need it. - Assist in identifying bottlenecks in the deployment pipeline and proposing process improvements. - Support communication and coordination between field teams, warehouse staff, and customers. - Help define and monitor KPIs related to deployment efficiency and on-time performance. - Contribute to documentation and standard operating procedures as the team scales into new markets. - Support ad hoc projects aimed at improving the speed and reliability of the deployment process.

jobs.title: Deployments Engineering Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE The Deployments Engineering team is responsible for the technical systems and standards that make Base installs safe, repeatable, and scalable—covering installation design, electrical and mechanical specifications, field diagnostics, and equipment performance. We solve the difficult, high-impact problems that determine whether a system goes into the ground correctly the first time. Joining this team means getting hands-on exposure to how hardware engineering translates into real homes, at scale. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Support the review and refinement of installation designs and technical specifications used by field crews. - Assist with troubleshooting technical issues that arise during deployment, from electrical faults to mechanical fit issues. - Help build and maintain documentation, checklists, and technical standards used across install crews. - Analyze field data to identify recurring issues and propose engineering or process improvements. - Support commissioning and quality-check processes to ensure systems meet performance and safety standards. - Coordinate with operations and field teams to translate engineering requirements into practical, on-the-ground execution. - Contribute to tooling or documentation that helps the engineering team scale its support across new markets.

jobs.title: Material Planning Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base designs its own hardware, builds it in its own factory, installs it at homes, and sells the power. That vertical integration is our advantage, and it means a single missing part can stop production. As a Material Planning Intern, you will own and plan material for a set of assigned parts, translate the production schedule into supply signals our suppliers can act on, and find shortages weeks before they reach the factory floor and coordinate with the manufacturing team. This is not a shadowing internship. You will be given parts to own, suppliers to talk to, and a production schedule that depends on you. The work sits between Manufacturing, Engineering, Procurement, Quality, and Logistics, and suits someone who thinks in systems, is comfortable acting on incomplete information, and likes building durable, robust processes. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own day-to-day material planning for assigned parts: run MRP, net demand against on-hand, on-order, and in-transit inventory, and keep purchase orders aligned to the build plan. - Turn the production plan into rolling forecasts for suppliers, then track what they committed to against what actually arrived. - Identify shortages and supply risk ahead of the floor, and escalate with the data behind it. - Support material readiness for engineering changes and new parts — phasing new material in and clearing old material out. - Dig into planning data: lead times, safety stock, order quantities, and supplier delivery performan

jobs.title: Business Operations Intern, Commercial Partnerships
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking an intern to join Base's Commercial Partnerships team, which supports the day-to-day success of our partners. These partnerships have introduced thousands of homeowners to Base and continue to scale rapidly each week. During your internship you'll be tasked with important problems for the business and expected to deliver just like any other full-time member of the team. You'll work on two fronts: supporting the day-to-day success of our existing partners, and helping target, analyze, and stand up new partnerships. On the existing side, that means market and competitive analysis, reporting, and problem-solving that keep our partners performing and motivated to win alongside us. On the new side, that means identifying prospective partners, building the business case for why a partnership makes sense, and helping get it off the ground. This is a foundational team that sees the entire lifecycle of a channel partnership and coordinates across sales, marketing, design, finance, product, deployment operations, and membership experience to make it work. You'll have direct visibility across the organization. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Support market and competitive analysis to identify and evaluate new partnership and market opportunities for the Commercial Partnerships team. - Build financial and business case models to size partnership opportunities, test assumptions, and support decisions. - Help design and track go-to-market plans for launching new partnerships

jobs.title: Fund Accounting Manager
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base finances its batteries partly through tax equity partnerships — structures that let outside investors fund a share of every battery we deploy in exchange for tax benefits and a return, while Base keeps building, installing, and running the fleet. As those funds scale, someone has to own the accounting inside each partnership: capital accounts, HLBV, allocations, and the books behind every K-1 and audit. That's this role. Base doesn't have a dedicated fund accounting function yet, and there's no existing playbook for it here — you'll build one. You'll set up the chart of accounts, close process, and reconciliation between fund-level and corporate books for Base's tax equity fund(s), then run that process as more funds come online. You'll work closely with the asset management and capital markets team on fund structuring and with corporate accounting on the tie-out between entities. As Base adds tax equity funds and other structured-finance vehicles, this role's scope grows with them. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own all fund-level accounting and financial reporting for Base's tax equity funds, including capital account maintenance, HLBV calculations, income and loss allocations, and distribution waterfall accounting. - Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual close process for each fund, ensuring accurate financial results and reconciliation between fund-level records and corporate accounting in NetSuite. - Prepare and maintain audit-ready accounting support, including

jobs.title: Payroll & Equity Adminstrator
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Base runs payroll for a growing, fully in-person team, and grants equity to employees who join. Both processes need someone who owns them fully and directly — not as a side responsibility bolted onto another role. This role processes payroll every cycle, ensures the payroll journal entry integration is properly mapped, prepares the payroll departmental allocations that feed the books, and administers Base's equity program end to end: grants, vesting, exercises, and cap table hygiene. You'll also support the transition to a new equity administration platform and own the accounting for stock-based compensation. You'll work closely with the broader accounting team on the entries that hit the books each period, with People on new hires, terminations, and comp changes, and with Finance office on equity grants and cap table questions. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Process payroll every cycle for Base's full employee population, including multi-state and hourly or field-team complexity. - Prepare payroll journal entries and departmental/cost-center allocations, and reconcile payroll to the general ledger each period. - Administer Base's equity program: process new grants, track vesting, process exercises, and keep the cap table and option ledger accurate. - Lead the transition from Base's current equity administration process to a new platform — data migration, testing, and employee-facing rollout. - Own stock-based compensation accounting: expense recognition, forfeitures, modifi

jobs.title: Business Operations, MBA Intern
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE The business operations team at Base is a lean group of generalists who take high-stakes, not-very-defined problems, give them structure, and drive them to completion. As our MBA intern, you'll get a real piece of that work for the summer, not a side project. You'll pick up a defined slice of whatever the team is running right now (today that's the integration of a recent acquisition; it could also be a commercial partnership or a market entry) and drive it to a decision. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Cover one part of the business for the summer: know its plan, its unit costs, and its tradeoffs better than anyone outside the team. - Own a discrete project inside it end to end — the forecast it runs on, a market or product entry, a workstream in an acquisition integration, or the scoreboard it's missing — and leave behind something that still runs without you. - Structure the problem yourself; define the goal, name the owners, write the memo that forces the tradeoff. - Build the analysis yourself — the model, the scoreboard, the one-pager — and defend the assumptions to the people who have to hit them. - Get into the data yourself; our warehouse, our install and market data, our AI tooling, rather than waiting on someone to pull it for you. - Work across functions without formal authority; rally owners in engineering, market operations, manufacturing, accounting, and customer operations. - Spend time where the money actually gets spent: ride along on an install, sit with ma

jobs.title: Supply Chain Intern - Procurement

As a GSM Intern, you will own sourcing for a set of assigned parts, run the RFQ process end to end, and negotiate cost and terms directly with suppliers. This is not a shadowing internship. You will be given parts to source, suppliers to negotiate with, and quotes that carry real weight in our build cost. jobs.title: Organic Social Content Intern

We’re hiring an Organic Social Content Manager to build Base into one of the most distinctive, entertaining, and trusted energy brands on social. You’ll own the day-to-day operation of Base’s organic channels, from developing the content calendar and creating original content to publishing, engaging with our audience, and learning from performance. jobs.description_text: About the Role Referrals are where care falls apart. A specialist referral leaves a primary care office as a fax, gets keyed into a queue by hand, waits on a phone call that nobody picks up, and lands back in an EHR days later with half the clinical context missing. Roughly a third never close the loop at all. Orchestrator is the product that fixes this. It ingests referrals however they arrive (fax, phone, direct EHR feed), extracts the clinical and demographic data, handles the outbound coordination work that today eats a coordinator's entire day, and writes the result back into the EHR of record. It is a mix of document AI, voice automation, and hard integration engineering, sitting on top of a full-stack product that referral coordinators live in for eight hours a day. We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team building it. This is an existing team with a shipping product and real customers, and you will grow it meaningfully over the next year. You will own delivery, drive the architecture decisions, and run your own hiring, working closely with the Director of Engineering on roadmap and prioritization. This is a good fit if you have a year or two of management under you, a deep engineering background, and you want the scope to grow quickly. jobs.title: Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations
jobs.description_text: THE OPPORTUNITY Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. THE ROLE As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems: - Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio. - Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios wit

jobs.description_text: Deepgram is looking for a Data Scientist to sit at the intersection between research and data: people who think deeply about what conversational data is actually composed of, what makes data valuable, and how to best leverage that. Conversational audio presents incredibly rich scientific, engineering, and infrastructure challenges that are orders of magnitude harder than working with text. Speech carries speakers, accents, dialects, emotion, overlapping talk, code-switching, domain vocabulary, and acoustic conditions that range from a quiet studio to a drive-through — all with rich context that moves the conversation. In this role you'll collaborate closely with our research, engineering, and data teams to answer those questions rigorously and at scale. You'll care deeply about what makes conversational data difficult, you'll characterize it, and you'll shape the strategies that turn it into model gains. This role rewards conviction, creativity in approach, and a real appetite for overturning your own assumptions when the data says otherwise. This is a hands-on, high-leverage role with unusual latitude to define an area from first principles. It reports to the VP of Data Operations. We're looking for people who: - See "we've always done it this way" as a starting position to argue with, not a constraint to work around - Can find the one experiment that settles a question in days rather than months - Are creative about where signal hides — in metadata, in model confidence, in

jobs.title: Applied ML Engineer -  Edge Devices
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Deepgram's speech models are among the fastest and most accurate in the world, and today we run them at scale on NVIDIA GPUs. Our customers increasingly need those same models on hardware we don't control: non-NVIDIA accelerators, edge servers, and embedded platforms with their own inference runtimes, operator sets, and constraints. Getting Deepgram models onto those platforms, with as few changes to the model as possible and no changes to the hardware paradigm, is the job. As an Applied ML Engineer on the Partner Platform Engineering team, you sit one layer above the metal. You take a Deepgram model as it exists today and adapt it to run correctly and efficiently within a target platform's existing kernel and runtime paradigm: swapping or reshaping operators, adjusting architecture parameters, choosing quantization and precision schemes, and validating accuracy and latency on the real device. Where a standard kernel isn't enough, you work with our Embedded AI Engineers, who write the custom kernels, and fit the model to what they build. You also own the deployment process that gets those adapted models onto edge targets repeatably. This is not a research role and not a cloud-serving role. It is applied ML for edge deployment. It is a great fit for a senior engineer who has already shipped models to non-GPU or edge hardware and wants to do it across many platforms, or a staff-level engineer who wants to define how Deepgram ports speech models to new hardware.
